problem.title: Business opportunity is often lost in translation.
problem.description: Businesses usually know the outcome they want. They do not always know the right provider category, capability term, procurement language, or evidence to request. Capable providers face the same problem in reverse.

items.title: “I know what I need—but not what to call it.”
items.detail: A business problem rarely arrives with the correct classification already attached.

items.title: “We can do the work—but customers describe it differently.”
items.detail: Similar capabilities can be expressed through different industries, services, and terminology.

items.title: “A directory tells me who exists—not always who fits.”
items.detail: Names, websites, and industry codes are useful, but they do not fully connect a specific need with the capability required.

items.title: “The context disappears as the process moves.”
items.detail: Email, spreadsheets, referrals, support programs, and bid systems often hold different pieces of the same need.

problem.closing: The RFxchange is designed to reduce that translation gap.

how.eyebrow: From ordinary language to market action
how.title: Start with what you know. The Exchange helps organize it.
how.description: You should not have to learn a classification system before explaining what your business needs or what it can provide.

amacs.title: A common language for market activity.
amacs.description: The RFxchange uses the Accel Market Activity and Capability Standard—AMACS—to connect more than what a business sells or which industry it belongs to.
amacs.support: AMACS gives the Exchange a common way to connect what the market needs with what organizations can actually do.

nodes.title: Need
nodes.detail: What is the market trying to accomplish?

nodes.title: Capability
nodes.detail: What must a provider be able to do?

nodes.title: Response
nodes.detail: What information does the market need back?

amacs.futureNote: Need and capability are central to the Exchange. RFx, decision, credibility, and outcome tools expand that same market context as they become available.

ai.title: AI can suggest. People confirm.
ai.description: AI can reduce the work of turning ordinary descriptions into structured market information. It may suggest relevant AMACS concepts and explain possible relationships, but a suggestion is not a market fact.
ai.highlight: You confirm what accurately represents your organization or business need before it becomes part of your Exchange information.
principles: Ordinary language is an acceptable starting point.
AI cannot silently add claims to your organization.
Rejected or unresolved suggestions do not change your organization information.
Manual AMACS browse and search remain available when assistance is disabled or unavailable.

network.title: See the market around your business.
network.description: Put your organization on the map, describe its capabilities, and become easier to discover through useful business context.

items.title: Find businesses by capability.

items.title: Use geography as business context.

items.title: Open the organization behind the marker.
items.detail: Move from location into useful capability, service, and organization information.

items.title: Move from discovery into action.
items.detail: Create referrals and provider connections without treating a connection itself as a successful outcome.

trust.title: Credibility should come from evidence—not payment.
trust.description: RFxchange keeps business claims, public-source information, provider status, verification, connections, commercial recognition, and outcomes distinct.
trust.highlight: Paid membership, Founding recognition, or sponsorship does not buy better capability matching, verification, qualification, or preferred placement in neutral discovery.
rules: A self-reported capability is not automatically verified.
Resource Provider status is not a guarantee of fit or availability.
A referral or provider connection is not a completed service or successful outcome.
Credibility and outcome signals should identify what supports them.

why.title: You do not have to wait for every Exchange feature to create value.
why.description: The first useful step is to make your organization understandable to the market. Clear capabilities and business context make discovery and future transactions more useful.

items.title: Establish your position early
items.detail: Create or claim your organization, confirm its geography, and build a useful capability profile.

items.title: Help shape practical workflows
items.detail: Use actual business conditions to show where terminology is confusing, information is burdensome, or connections need better context.

items.title: Contribute to a better market language

items.title: Be recognized as part of the launch cohort
items.detail: Founding Organization recognition records early participation. It is not verification, qualification, endorsement, or superior performance.

scenario.eyebrow: The problem we are building around
scenario.title: Business owners should not need procurement expertise to explain a business need.
scenario.quote: “We have outgrown the way we manage inventory and need help figuring out a better system.”
scenario.description: That statement may involve process analysis, inventory technology, systems integration, data migration, training, workflow design, or several capabilities together. RFxchange lets the business begin with the problem it understands and then organize the useful details.

standard.title: AI helps with the translation. AMACS provides the structure. People confirm what is true.
standard.description: AMACS connects Need, Capability, Evidence, Response, Decision, and Outcome. AI may suggest relevant concepts, but it does not decide what your company can do or declare another organization qualified.
standard.highlight: Suggestions reduce the work. People confirm the business facts.

boundaries.title: Money does not make a business a better match.

items.title: No pay-to-rank
items.detail: Founding status does not move an organization above a more relevant participant in neutral discovery.

items.title: No pay-to-verify
items.detail: Membership does not establish that a capability, credential, or business claim is true.

items.title: No pay-to-qualify
items.detail: Founding status cannot substitute for the requirements of a particular opportunity.

items.title: No guaranteed business
items.detail: RFxchange does not guarantee leads, referrals, contracts, revenue, awards, financing, or growth.

boundaries.closing: Commercial benefits and market truth remain separate by design.

items.question: Do I need to know how to write an RFP?
items.answer: No. RFxchange is broader than formal procurement. You can begin with the need you understand, and RFx workflows can add transaction structure where it is useful.

items.question: Do I need to understand AMACS codes?
items.answer: No. You may browse structured concepts, but ordinary-language assistance and explanations are designed to make the standard useful without memorizing a taxonomy.

items.question: Does Founding participation make my business Verified?
items.answer: No. Founding Organization is launch-cohort recognition. Verification is a separate process based on the information being verified.

items.question: Will Founding membership improve my search ranking?
items.answer: No. Payment does not change substantive capability information, neutral matching, qualification, or credibility.

items.question: Is the $49 membership active now?
items.answer: The page will identify enrollment as available when billing and the included Founding benefits are ready to use.

cta.title: Establish your organization now. Choose deeper participation when it is ready for you.
cta.description: Start with the useful free organization experience, then move into Founding participation when enrollment is available.
cta.note: Founding recognition does not buy verification, qualification, preferred ranking, or guaranteed business.
